verified.exploit_entry_point: The fabio binary's own listeners: an HTTP request through the request handler and reverse proxy, and a gRPC call through the transparent gRPC handler wired in main.go. Hidden tests start the real binary with a static routing table, send raw HTTP/1.1 or gRPC metadata over loopback, and read what the backend received, so any valid fix layer (configuration wiring, request handling, or the transport) is exercised the way an operator would exercise it.
sites: proxy/http_headers.go:39-53 (header builder sets the forwarding headers; no declaration filtering)
proxy/http_proxy.go:88-94 (request id set in the handler, outside the header builder)
proxy/http_handler.go:18-32 (stock httputil.ReverseProxy removes hop-by-hop tokens after the headers are set)
config/load.go:149-152 (clientip, tls and requestid names come from operator flags)
proxy/grpc_handler.go:52-58 (client metadata copied verbatim to the outgoing context)
main.go:178 (gRPC listener uses the transparent handler; the header builder never runs)
routes: T2: an operator-named client-address header and an operator-named request-id header declared hop-by-hop by the client and carrying a client value
T3: the operator-named request id written in the request handler, declared hop-by-hop
T4: the operator designates the well-known client-address header and the client supplies a value for it
T6: gRPC metadata carrying client values for the client-address, request-id and transport-assertion headers
verified.project_tests_run: go test ./proxy -count=1 -run 'TestAddHeaders|TestAddResponseHeaders|TestLocalPort|TestUint16Base16|TestProxyProducesCorrectXForwardedSomethingHeader|TestProxyRequestIDHeader' at image build on the pinned tree
verified.not_routes_at_pinned: T1 (the reported route) is covered by five security tests but is not a lever. T5 (raw websocket forwarding) needs a hop-by-hop-honouring intermediary and is kept as must-keep functional coverage. T7 (a declaration split across several lines) was checked behaviourally: a first-value parser drops the whole declaration and therefore blocks the attack, so it is kept as a functional case rather than a security lever.

traps.shape: the client-address and transport header names come from operator configuration, so a filter built from the fixed well-known forwarding names leaves the configured names removable; coupled must-keep-working: the designated header is still set on ordinary requests and the address chain keeps appending
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the reported header is one of the well-known forwarding names, so a list of those names looks complete
traps.realistic_because: published fix far site (GHSA-fq95-v8xc-jm3v): the second advisory protects exactly the operator-named headers the first fix missed

traps.shape: the request id is written in the request handler, outside the header builder, and reads as a correlation value rather than a trust header
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a request id is a correlation value, not security data, and it is set where the other forwarding headers are not built
traps.realistic_because: published fix far site (GHSA-fq95-v8xc-jm3v): the first fix's list covers only well-known forwarding names and never names the request id

traps.shape: when the operator designates the well-known client-address header, the pinned code still skips writing it and keeps a client-supplied value; the same path deliberately preserves a client value for the undesignated default, pinned by a project unit test
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the project preserves a client-supplied value on purpose for chained proxies and a unit test pins it, so leaving that header alone looks correct
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the skip and the conditional write predate the advisory and both published fixes

traps.shape: the transparent gRPC path copies every client metadata entry to the outgoing context and never derives the trust values at all
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the gRPC proxy is a transparent metadata pass-through that never set derived headers, so it reads as a missing feature rather than a vulnerable route
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the verbatim metadata copy is still present after both published fixes

wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the proxy only writes request headers for the backend; there is no read/write split to miss
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the declaration filter runs before the reverse proxy consumes the header, and no adjusting step follows it
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the values are derived locally from the connection; there is no authority or secret lookup that can return nothing
wrong_fix_catalogue.adjacent_api: n/a: the fix touches only unexported request-header handling; no exported sibling API changes behaviour
